id: # Known gaps of the conformance suite: every check that fails today, keyed by root cause.
# A test family fails when a check fails without a row here, when a row's class changes, or when a
# row matches nothing any more: a change that fixes a gap deletes its rows. See
# tests/conformance/support/ratchet.rs for the columns.
# Root causes (TS1-TS26 from the test-suite plan section 4; TS27-TS34 added with the suite, TS35 with the typed model,
# TS36-TS37 with the conversion between versions, TS38 with GEDCOM 7.0.18):
# TS1  CR-only line terminators are fatal, in every encoding
# TS2  an extension tag after CONT/CONC, after a pointer citation or under a NOTE is fatal
# TS3  extension, unknown or non-standard enumeration values are fatal
# TS4  a FAM with a second HUSB or WIFE is fatal
# TS5  blank lines and text lines without a level are fatal
# TS6  an xref on a substructure is fatal
# TS7  a pointer-shaped payload containing a space is fatal
# TS8  a second GEDC.FORM is fatal
# TS9  bytes that contradict HEAD.CHAR, or a character set it names, are fatal or decoded with the wrong table
# TS10 an ANSEL combining mark at a CONC split is fatal
# TS11 a lone CR inside an LF file drops the next line
# TS12 repeated {0:M} substructures keep only the last; duplicate links are merged
# TS13 standard structures, PHRASEs and records lost on read or write
# TS14 invalid or unusual values (ages, coordinates) dropped or rewritten on read
# TS15 the leading space of a payload is dropped
# TS16 CONT/CONC bound to the wrong structure, or written after substructures or at a space
# TS17 7.0 output carries GEDC.FORM and HEAD.CHAR
# TS18 5.5.1 output keeps the input's CHAR label over UTF-8 text
# TS19 7.0 enumeration values written in lower case
# TS20 `@` not escaped on write (7.0 leading @@, 5.5.1 every @), text written as a pointer
# TS21 line length: 5.5.1 lines over 255 characters, 7.0 payloads split with CONC
# TS22 banned control characters written raw
# TS23 invalid, duplicate or @VOID@ xrefs written as they were read
# TS24 the writer invents NAME pieces absent from the input
# TS25 conversion between 5.5.1 and 7.0 is incomplete (values, structures and records not converted)
# TS26 reference validation reports @VOID@ as dangling
# TS27 5.5.1 records over 32K made of structures, not text (the test files' `date-all`: individuals with 1,296 births):
#      no note can move out of them, nor can a record be split; 5.5.1 only recommends the limit (p.10)
# TS28 5.5.1 network pointers (`:`, `!`) are not kept as pointers
# TS29 non-date escape sequences (`@#...@`) are not kept verbatim
# TS30 ANSEL is not decoded to NFC across the full repertoire (stacked marks included)
# TS31 GEDCOM 7.1 is not supported as a write target
# TS32 the last line is written without a terminator
# TS33 the written header is not synthesised for the target (5.5.1 SOUR/SUBM, GEDC.VERS, FORM)
# TS34 values and structures the target does not allow are written verbatim (no conformance repair)
# TS35 a conformance case's input that the specification does not permit (a 7.0 day past its month's end, a value outside a
#      closed set, an extension tag documented as a record type): the conformance repair (spec::conform, run by the writer
#      on every write) rewrites it, while the case expects it verbatim. Leniency cases accept the repaired forms
#      (tests/conformance/support/semantic.rs, `lost`), so their invalid input has no such row.
# TS36 an expected conversion of the gedcom7code test files that no converter can match: it rewrites texts its input does
#      not (`date-all` NOTEs: `ROMAN 28` expected as `_ROMAN 28`), keeps 7.0-invalid dates verbatim (31 NOV, 13 COMP 25:
#      TS35), resolves the same invalid dual years two ways (`date-all`: the year written; `date-dual-invalid`: the
#      nearest year with the digits after the slash) and valid ones to the year written where the migration guide takes
#      the later one (`21 FEB 366/7`), or drops a dangling pointer (`xref-case`: `@test@` as `@VOID@`) that the writer
#      keeps as an extension.
# TS37 GEDCOM 5.5.1 has no time zone: a 7.x time in UTC (`11:11:11Z`) is written as its clock time.
# TS38 a test file with a pointer cycle 7.x prohibits: a shared note citing the source that points to it, a SOUR-SNOTE cycle
#      that 7.0 already prohibited and 7.0.17 restates beside the SOUR-OBJE one (gedcom7code and FamilySearch `notes-1`'s
#      and `notes71`'s "cyclic note record"; FamilySearch's `maximal70`, whose @N1@ cites @S1@, which points to @N1@: the
#      SOUR-OBJE loops were taken out of it, GEDCOM.io #368 and #395, this one was not). The writer cuts the pointer that
#      closes the cycle in the order it writes the records (spec::graph): the shared note's `_SOUR` from a tree, the
#      source's `_SNOTE`s from the typed model, which writes notes before sources. The vendored 7.0 file is a leniency
#      case (tests/conformance/vendored.rs), its round trip compared as such.
